summary: New box Part. Pass.: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (Jan 2.35/5515)

data.turoyo: Ǧan: Abuna gədmšayalnolox šəwolo, ġalabe muhim, adyawme ste i ṣərtayḏe heš aʕlayna bṣəmto, ršəmto yo.
data.translation: Jan: Father, I am going to ask you a question, a very important one; today too its picture is still imprinted on us, drawn there.

rationale: New Detransitive sense 1 and Part. Pass. box; feminine image subject and overt yo show the figurative impressed state. No edition translation is available.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 3.28/722)

data.turoyo: <...> Lo, mṣalənwa aʕle bi ʕito w bi ʕito gədrəšmiwaynale w bəṯr mu ršomo hedi gədmaydiwayle. <...>
data.translation: Archpriest Aziz: No, they would pray over him in the church, and in the church we would mark him with the cross, and a little after the signing they would lift him. They would take him and bury him. If he was a priest, they would wash his feet and his hands too. And if he was not a priest, if he was a layman, likewise.

rationale: New I Infectum-wa box; first-plural -wayna- and deceased patient -le in a church ritual. The precise sign is not named. No edition translation is available.

summary: New sense 1: (mit ʕal) fig. eingeprägt, eingezeichnet sein (Detrans.)
rationale: An image i ṣərtayḏe is ršəmto yo aʕlayna, coordinated with bṣəmto. This is a retained impression on people, distinct from giving names or making a cross. One attestation; only the state formation is proposed, without inventing an active drawing sense.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (JTM 4.2/4)

data.turoyo: maʕmaḏḏe u zʕuro b əšme d Mšiḥo w ršəmme bayne ʕayne w yatu axile aʕmayye.
data.translation: sie tauften den Jungen im Namen des Messias und machten das (Kreuz)zeichen auf seiner Stirn. Dann setzte er sich hin und aß mit ihnen.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell: bodily site bayne ʕayne and omitted sign-object in a baptism scene.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (97/9)

data.turoyo: ʕAl at təšʕo yarḥe l aloho hulele abro. “Eh”, — u malko omər, — “ma grošamle w ma lo?”
data.translation: Nach neun Monaten schenkte ihm Gott einen Sohn. Der König sprach: Nun, wer soll ihm einen Namen geben und wer nicht?

rationale: Thin Infectum cell: newborn and explicit question about who will name him.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (97/10)

data.turoyo: Omər aṯi u waziro Titəlyos, məlle: “Eh, ya u wazir! Annaqla u zʕurano, hat d rəšmatle.” Maḥatle əšme du kurrəkayḏe, du abro du malko, Qambar Zaman.
data.translation: Als der Wesir Titiliyos kam, sprach er: Nun, Wesir, jetzt mußt du dem Knaben einen Namen geben. Der Wesir gab dem Knaben, dem Sohne des Königs, den Namen Qambar Zaman.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell: second-person form and explicit subsequent name assignment.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Jan 2.16/3557)

data.turoyo: W maḥətte muklo qume, d kətyo huwe mniʕo mu muklano. Elo bu ḥaylo du ṣlibo qadišo, d rsəmle aʕle, mbadəl u muklo, hawi yariquṯo, gelo yaʕni.
data.translation: And they put food before him, from which food he was abstaining. But through the power of the holy cross, which he traced over it, the food changed, became vegetables, greens, that is.

rationale: Thin I.1 Preterit cell; explicit holy-cross antecedent and aʕle target support the round-1 cross-signing construction despite source rsəmle. No edition translation is available.

summary: Sense 1: revise the gloss
after: einen Namen geben; ein Kreuz schlagen (mit ṣlibo, auch ohne genanntes Zeichen);
rationale: The inherited geben, schlagen omits the semantic content. Existing 97/10 and 94/48 establish naming; the existing camel Preterit explicitly has ṣlibo and JTM 4.2/4 supplies bodily signing. Clarify both already represented meanings without renumbering.

summary: New idiom: ršəmle/rošəm ṣlibo l- 'ein Kreuz über etwas schlagen'

data.headword: ršəmle/rošəm ṣlibo l- 'ein Kreuz über etwas schlagen'
data.turoyo: Həzla raġla li gamlo laf qarʕa, ršəmla ṣlibo l foṯa w mʕamaṣla ʕayna.
data.translation: Das Kamel bewegte den Fuss gegen den Kopf hin, schlug ein Kreuz über's Gesicht und schloss die Augen.

rationale: Phrase index for an established construction already in this entry’s Preterit. Search ṣlibo found the same ršm quotation and parallel dry/ṭrḥ uses, but no existing idiom-list headword under ršm; this is newly indexed, not a claim of a newly discovered sense.

summary: The existing single gloss compresses naming and cross-signing. Both are now stated explicitly under the unchanged number 1; the established ṣlibo construction is also indexed under Idiomatic phrases.

Naming takes a suffixed child patient in Infectum, with an explicit maḥatle əšme reformulation in 97/10. Cross-signing has an overt ṣlibo object plus l- bodily site in the camel story; JTM 4.2/4 omits the sign noun and gives bayne ʕayne.

MAC Besim History of Bsorino/12 sequences ršəmle, baptism and maḥatle bəšme Dawiḏ. This permits a ritual interpretation but does not independently disambiguate signing and naming. Keep it out of the selected examples.
Read-only search of ṣlibo located the exact ršm context, parallel dry phrase and ṭrḥ cross-signing sense. None justifies conflating ršm with the distinct rsm ordination root.

Jan Beṯ-Şawoce provides no edition translation. English in the input is machine translation and is not quoted as an edition translation. Added examples therefore have an empty translation field; meanings are assessed from the Turoyo.
Round 1's clarified active gloss and ṣlibo collocation are retained. Jan contributes a new Detransitive impressed-image state, not another active gloss replacement.

The permitted full rsm lookup contains ordination and its Detransitive, with no picture-impression sense. Source s/š alone cannot decide a root, but the overt cross at Jan 2.16/3557 supports ršm rather than ordination.
The funeral passage supplies both Infectum-wa and Infinitiv for ritual marking. A corpse is the patient; this is not appointing a living cleric.
The figurative impression is predicated of an image and located aʕlayna. No drawing agent or active drawing predicate is present.
In MAC Besim History of Bsorino/12, does ršəmle mean cross-signing, the naming rite before baptism, or a broader ritual action? The English alone is insufficient.
Should editors eventually split the two clarified meanings? Existing examples share sense 1, so this proposal retains their number pending a deliberate reorganisation.
What precise rite/sign is called rəšm-/ršomo in Jan 3.28/722? Is it always cross-signing?
Confirm whether ršəmto yo at Jan 2.35/5515 belongs to inherited ršm or a contact-influenced drawing/marking formation.
Can the Infinitiv ršomo be retained under active I as its event nominal, rather than an inconsistently used historical Detransitive heading?
Signing over food and ritual marking of the deceased support the cross-signing/marking component clarified in round 1. The former supports the existing ṣlibo idiom; neither is a new idiom.
